newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pechiney sees lower 1996 net earnings.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney sees lower 1996 net earnings.

text.p: Metals group Pechiney SA said on Thursday that it expected net earnings for full-year 1996 to be lower than 1995 on a pro forma basis.

"Based on current information, the group believes that net earnings for the full-year 1996, before taking into account the costs related to the Challenge project, will not reach the level of 1995 earnings on a pro forma basis (i.e. 732 million francs)," the company said in a statement.
The company said first-half net income fell to 426 million francs from 658 million francs.

Pechiney said it had identified potential cost reductions in its Challenge cost-cutting programme for an estimated total of four billion francs on a yearly basis or 20 percent of direct costs, excluding raw materials.
The first stage of the new Challenge cost-cutting drive is to be implemented by the end of 1998.
Pechiney said along with these savings, investments of approximately 3.5 billion francs will be made over the next three years.
It said the plan would also involve spending of about two billion francs over the same period for restructuring and other expenses involved in the plan's implementation.

It said these expenses are not reflected in the first half financial statements but a large portion of the expenses along with potential asset writeoffs will be "reserved for at year-end 1996 after the plan becomes effective and the related reserve is assessed."
